summary:
The SL-091 build does what the design says. `ShellReveal.Walk` (src/FsAnalyser.Core/Native/ShellReveal.cs:275-337) now reads the target's own attributes before the open. For a Hidden target that is not a volume root, it reads Explorer's view once through `SHGetSetSettings(…, 0x00040001, false)`. If that view hides the item, Walk returns Failed / HiddenByExplorerSettings with HResult 0, with `HiddenBy` and `View` set, and never calls the open. The pidl is still freed by the same finally. Order of checks: unaddressable name, then parse failure, then parsed-as-another-item, then the new refusal, then open failure, then Exact. Neither the Walk delegate nor any folder above the item is consulted except as designed. `FormatRevealStatus` (MainWindow.xaml.cs:858-883) puts the outcome and the leaf first. The old blanket note is gone; a grep finds it only in the design note. The override is hide-only (`Effective` = real AND mask). The hook arms it before Main and throws on format/type/member/invoke failures.

What I ran, all on this PC:
- Focused Core tests (ShellReveal, ArchitectureRules, ExplorerSettingsWriteRule, RuleCopiesAgree): 199/199 passed.
- Full suite: 689/692. The 3 failures are the known last-access tests (HeldOpenTreeTests ×2, LastAccessTests ×1), not reveal tests.
- Fitness op=check: 85 rules, all hold.
- rules-parity: AGREE, 18 facts / 22 twinned / 48 patterns, 63 settled.
- `WindowCases -Case R-003`: PASSED in 19 s. (a) five targets refused under injected 0|0 with the exact texts, including the 200-character name that equals the B-007 pin. (b) `2|x` refused before Main, exit 0xE0434352. (c) pagefile.sys refused from a C:\ scan stopped at the root listing. (d) under the real (1,0) settings, hs_file.sys and hs_dir refused for ProtectedFiles only; the H-only targets reported owed to a person. No Explorer window opened.
- `WindowMutants -Mutant NoExplorerViewMember`: PASSED in 30 s. R-003 failed only on the armed check in (a) and (c), with reason=member. ShellReveal.cs was restored byte for byte.
- `WindowCases -Case B-007`: PASSED. At 560x644 the status line is one line of 15.96 px; the text is 1223.91 px untrimmed in 512 px, and 141 of 323 characters show.
- C:\ itself reads Hidden, System, Directory, so the volume-root test really feeds a root that would otherwise be refused.

Every case-matrix test I read feeds its shape: real temp items with the stated attributes, a deny-all +H+S folder whose listing is proven denied, the real System Volume Information plus each Hidden+System *.sys at C:\ through the real parse, and plain items under +H and +H+S folders.

One defect: the write-guard class that O-044 declared closed is missing a member. An `OpenSubKey` of Explorer\Advanced asking for write rights through the `RegistryRights` overload gets past rule B and rule C. I checked it with the rule's own regex.

One extra: open failure on a visible Hidden item has no test.

One undeclared drift, noted below: the twinned rules carry Fact-style names, not the design's.

No loop on this slice: one build attempt. The two earlier code-review records are a provider turn-away and an empty record.

Second round: Second pass over the same tree, this time trying to break each new reader, matcher and boundary. I found one new problem, and it is in the instructions handed to the person, not in the code.

The new readers and matchers hold up, or fail loudly when given input they don't expect:
- **The `SettledPatterns` reader in ExplorerSettingsWriteRuleTests.** It splits lines on CRLF, LF or a lone CR. A quoted or commented rule name, a trailing YAML comment, or a pattern quoted differently stops the read and turns the 9- and 6-pattern count assertions red. A second block with the same name is read first-wins, and the plants would expose it.
- **The `FSA_HOOK_EXPLORER_VIEW` parser.** Whitespace or anything that is not exactly 0 or 1 is refused before Main, so it fails closed.
- **The `StatusFit` binary search.** A zero width gives fits 0, and the check then fails.
- **The `ExplorerView` decode.** It reads a zeroed 64-byte buffer, little-endian.
- **Walk's boundaries.** `explorer()` throwing is caught by RevealAsync's catch, and the pidl is still freed. An attribute read that throws is narrow: .NET falls back to the parent's listing on access-denied and on sharing violations, as the real pagefile.sys test shows. A forward-slash path cannot reach the reveal, because LongPath.cs:41 normalises roots with GetFullPath.
- **The volume-root exemption.** It covers drive, SUBST and share roots.
- **The R-003 JSON comparisons.** A null view and a null injected value are compared correctly.

I checked the engine's fitness.py: .ps1 gets only `#` line blanking, with no `<# #>` block handling. That makes rule C's 'a commented example cannot trip it' slightly overclaimed, but tests/window has no block comments today and the failure would be a loud false positive, so I did not file it.

The new finding: the design note's person sitting tells the owner to re-run the 0/13 Explorer-selection measurement through the shipped exe (R-001 and R-003). That exe now refuses every hidden target before any open (ShellReveal.cs:318-323). The same applies to the spike-92 harness, which compiles the live ShellReveal.cs: its X1 row now gets a refusal instead of the open it is meant to observe. So one owner sitting with Explorer's settings changed cannot settle the build-check's open item, 'Claimed measurement 0 of 13: unknown', with the steps as written.

findings.claim:
The write guards the build declared closed as a class (O-044, ExplorerSettingsWriteCorpus.json) let through an ordinary writable open of Explorer\Advanced. Their OpenSubKey pattern treats the key as writable only if `true` or `ReadWriteSubTree` follows on the line. The documented .NET overload `OpenSubKey(string, RegistryRights)`, and `OpenSubKey(string, RegistryKeyPermissionCheck.Default, RegistryRights)`, open the key with SetValue/WriteKey/FullControl rights and match neither. I fed three such lines through rule B's six patterns and every one got 0 hits:
- `Registry.CurrentUser.OpenSubKey(@"Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced", RegistryRights.SetValue);`
- the same with `RegistryKeyPermissionCheck.Default, RegistryRights.FullControl`;
- `RegistryKey.OpenBaseKey(...).OpenSubKey(..., RegistryRights.WriteKey)`.
Rule C over tests/window carries the same OpenSubKey pattern (fitness.yaml:1126), so the PowerShell spelling `[System.Security.AccessControl.RegistryRights]::SetValue` gets past it too. These are not pinned as known misses in the corpus, so the class is not closed as the build claimed. A src or window-script write of Hidden through such a key would pass dotnet test, Fitness and the corpus test alike.
findings.evidence: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/ArchitectureRulesTests.cs:282 (twin of .taad/fitness.yaml:282); .taad/fitness.yaml:1126 (rule C). Probe run in pwsh against the Fact's patterns: 0 hits on each RegistryRights line. The corpus (ExplorerSettingsWriteCorpus.json B07-B10, B28-B29, W16) has no RegistryRights row.
findings.fix:
In both OpenSubKey patterns (fitness.yaml:282 and its Fact at ArchitectureRulesTests.cs:282, and fitness.yaml:1126), widen the write marker from `\b(true|ReadWriteSubTree)\b` to `\b(true|ReadWriteSubTree|RegistryRights\]?(\.|::)(SetValue|WriteKey|FullControl|CreateSubKey))\b`. Add these corpus rows:
- B30 src fire: `        using var key = Registry.CurrentUser.OpenSubKey(@"Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced", RegistryRights.SetValue);`
- B31 src fire: the same with `RegistryKeyPermissionCheck.Default, RegistryRights.FullControl`
- B32 src quiet: the same with `RegistryRights.ReadKey`
- W35 window fire: `$adv = [Microsoft.Win32.Registry]::CurrentUser.OpenSubKey('Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced', [System.Security.AccessControl.RegistryRights]::SetValue)`
Then rerun rules-parity and harness --only for the touched plants.

findings.claim: There is a branch the matrix does not list: an open that fails after the gate has passed a Hidden item, for example H-only at 1|0 and SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems returning E_FAIL. The design's contract names it ('An open failure after a visible verdict gives Failed / None with that hr'), and the build changed what it carries (declared deviation: Hidden, System and View now ride on it). No test reaches it. The only open-failure test, Walk_OpenFails_RefusesWithItsCodeFreesTheIdListAndTriesNothingElse, walks the nonexistent C:\a\b.txt, so the attribute read throws, the item counts as not hidden and View stays null. A regression that, say, dropped View or reported HiddenByExplorerSettings on this branch would stay green.

findings.claim:
The design note's 'one Hidden=2 sitting a person owes' assumes the shipped exe can still re-measure what Explorer selects for hidden items at Windows defaults. After this build it cannot.

1. Step 3 says 'Re-run the 0/13 measurement through the shipped exe (WindowCases.ps1 -Case R-001 and -Case R-003)'. At Hidden=2, Walk refuses every Hidden and Hidden+System target before the open (ShellReveal.cs:318-323). R-001 step 5 and R-003 step (d) would then log refusals and open no window. Nothing re-measures 'Explorer opened the parent and selected 0 of 13'.
2. Step 3's 'adding C:\Program Files\WindowsApps and System-only items, with every control logging its full path and each ancestor's attributes' names nothing that either case can do. Neither case has such a target or such logging.
3. Step 2 runs the spike-92 harness, which compiles the live src ShellReveal.cs and calls RevealAsync. Its non-hidden ancestor rows are still measured. Its X1 row (+H file in a +H folder) will now be refused rather than open the folder, so that row records 'no window', not the predicate-table fact it exists for.

The consequence: the one sitting in which the owner changes Explorer's settings would leave the build-check's open 'Claimed measurement: 0 of 13 … unknown' unmeasured, while the record says a sitting covers it.
findings.evidence: docs/design/SL-091-hidden-reveal-refuses.md:96-107 (the sitting). src/FsAnalyser.Core/Native/ShellReveal.cs:318-323 (the refusal before open). tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 Test-R003 step (d) and Test-R001 step 5 (refusals only, no Explorer read).
findings.fix:
Reword step 3 of the sitting:
- Through the shipped exe (R-001 step 5, R-003 (d)), the sitting confirms only that hidden targets are refused at Hidden=2.
- The Explorer-selection re-measurement (0/13, WindowsApps, X1) needs a harness that opens without the gate. That is either the spike-74 run.ps1, which calls SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems itself, or a harness that compiles ShellReveal.cs and calls Walk with an explorer delegate returning ExplorerView(true, true).
- Say that spike-92's X1 row, built against the current ShellReveal.cs, is now refused and needs that same bypass.

drift: The twinned rules A and B are in .taad/fitness.yaml:267-286 under Fact-style names, 'OnlyShellRevealReadsOrOverridesExplorersViewSettings (*.cs)' and 'TheAppNeverWritesExplorersSettings (*.cs)'. The design declared them as 'only ShellReveal.cs reads or overrides Explorer's view settings' and 'the app never writes Explorer's settings'. The yaml comment and the design note explain the twinning, but the rename is not in the declared deviations. Review n1 recorded the engine appending declared rules only when no entry of that name exists. If the engine reconciles this design's architecture_rules by name again, it would find A and B absent. It would then append settled copies, which would STRAY-HIT plants F41-F48 and change the settled count (63).

Nothing else departs undeclared. The other departures I found (wider rule B and rule C patterns, R-001's added h_file.dat, R-003(b)'s H+S target, the extra CheckStatusShown assertion, the label without '(Recommended)', Hidden/System/View on the open-failure outcome, ExplorerView as a record class, the Windows 10 limit kept only in the design note) are all in the build's deviations list.
